claim.statement: By 1 May 2026, current official and domestic reporting showed Iran's higher-education disruption remained war-bound and only partially reopening: SNN reported the science minister saying war required basic reconsideration of policy, educational programs, the university calendar, and admissions; EghtesadOnline/Vista reported final exams and Konkur timing tied to official announcement of the war's end; and the Sharif reopening signal remained limited to PhD students from 14 Ordibehesht for research progress.
claim.subject: Iran's higher-education system
claim.object: war-bound with calendar/testing uncertainty and restricted reopening

evidence.summary: Existing SNN source says the science minister called war a higher-education turning point requiring reconsideration of policy, programs, university calendar, and admission capacity.
EghtesadOnline/Vista reports that final exams and Konkur timing were made conditional on the official announcement of the war's end.
Existing AsrIran source records Sharif University reopening only for PhD students from Monday 14 Ordibehesht to continue research work.

information_depth.rationale: The claim rests on named domestic reports, ministry-level language, a testing/calendar article, and a university-specific partial reopening notice.

claim.statement: A completed 1-2 May 2026 xPool campus query kept student-control stress visible but still did not show a broad verified campus protest or strike cluster: among 120 emitted items, the strongest repression signal was a 1 May high-engagement post saying students were being summoned over pre-war gatherings and asked for online/email defenses without a charge-explanation session under internet-cutoff visibility; other items complained about possible Saturday in-person reopening, attendance-consent forms, in-person practical/project/internship courses, and student life disruption.
claim.subject: Persian X campus-control discourse
claim.object: student summons and forced-reopening complaints without a broad verified campus mobilization cluster

evidence.summary: The completed xPool dataset includes tweet 2050108746274066511 about student summons for pre-war gatherings, plus scattered reopening and internet disruption complaints; it did not form a broad verified protest cluster.
The source notes record the 120-item sample, relevant high-engagement posts, and the manual read that most items were noisy dorm/university chatter or generic internet and war commentary.

information_depth.rationale: The xPool job completed and the summons post is high-engagement with an image, but social posts do not independently verify identities, campus notices, or disciplinary case files.

assessment.uncertainty: Needs primary student-channel posts, official university disciplinary notices, family/lawyer statements, or release/detention follow-up to verify the summons pattern.

claim.statement: The 1 May 2026 Exa/Vista campus-unrest search lane is contaminated by older student-unrest material: the Khabarfoori/Vista 'tense reopening after 56 days' result has a fresh Vista wrapper date, but the article body is dated 1404/12/04 and the image path is 2026-02-23, referring to the earlier Dey-to-Esfand closure; related Vista sidebars surface older or ambiguous student-gathering and KNTU-clash headlines that should not be treated as current May 2026 evidence without direct article-body confirmation.
claim.subject: May 2026 campus-unrest search results
claim.object: contaminated by old or ambiguous Vista-aggregated student-unrest reports

evidence.summary: The Khabarfoori/Vista body carries source date 1404/12/04 and an image dated 2026-02-23 despite a May 1 Vista wrapper date; its 56-day closure framing points to the older Dey-to-Esfand reopening.
The notes record the Exa result set and the caution that Vista sidebars and wrappers resurfaced older or ambiguous campus-unrest headlines.

information_depth.rationale: The article body date, image path date, and event framing all indicate an old report despite current wrapper metadata.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v35 - campus stress is controlled reopening, not verified fresh protest
synthesis.summary: The thirty-fifth pass revisits the campus lane after fresh searches surfaced apparently current student-unrest headlines. The high-confidence current crack is administrative control and uncertainty: the science minister says war requires reconsidering policy, programs, calendar, and admissions; EghtesadOnline/Vista says final exams and Konkur timing are tied to the official end of war; and Sharif's concrete reopening is still only PhD students from 14 Ordibehesht for research progress. A completed 120-item xPool campus sample adds a live repression signal: a high-engagement May 1 post says students are being summoned over pre-war gatherings while internet disruption suppresses visibility, and asked for online/email defenses without a charge-explanation session. It also shows complaints about Saturday in-person reopening and attendance/consent forms. But it still does not show a broad verified new campus protest or strike cluster. Search hygiene is the guardrail: Vista made an older Khabarfoori '56-day tense reopening' article look current even though the body date is 1404/12/04 / 2026-02-23. Net: student pressure is real, but the visible May 1-2 pattern is controlled reopening plus disciplinary pressure, not a confirmed open campus wave.
synthesis.limitations: The disciplinary summons signal is social-media evidence, not primary case documentation. The xPool query is useful for visible discourse topology but cannot see suppressed channels or private campus networks. Vista aggregation can distort dates, so current campus-protest claims need direct article-body dates, student-channel archives, family/lawyer statements, or official notices.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis combines current official/domestic articles, a completed xPool dataset, existing KNB campus rows, and explicit source-hygiene checks.

operations.rationale: The claim directly updates whether virtual-class, dorm-closure, and restricted reopening pressures are becoming a normalized post-war campus model.
The xPool social signal specifically concerns student summons and possible post-war disciplinary reprisals, while preserving the uncertainty around scale.
Complaints about Saturday in-person reopening, attendance forms, and practical-course attendance are part of the restricted campus model question.
The source-hygiene finding prevents old student-unrest reports from being misread as fresh evidence for a coordinated post-war crackdown.
The named-student verification question needs primary current records because aggregate search results can surface old or ambiguous campus-unrest material.

operations.reason: v35 updates the active read from market stress to the campus lane: fresh searches show controlled reopening and disciplinary pressure, but not a verified new campus protest cluster, and source hygiene blocks old Vista-aggregated unrest reports from being misread as current.
